trials.name: Clarity AD
trials.population: Male and female participants aged 50-90 with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease and confirmed brain amyloid pathology
trials.primary_endpoint: Core Study: Change from Baseline in the CDR-SB at 18 Months
trials.results_summary: The core 18-month study met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a highly statistically significant 27% slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB compared to placebo. It also met all key secondary endpoints, including significant clearance of brain amyloid.

trials.name: Study 201
trials.primary_endpoint: Core Study Phase: Change From Baseline in Alzheimer's Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS) at Month 12
trials.results_summary: Established target engagement (robust amyloid reduction) and potential clinical efficacy at the highest tested dose (10 mg/kg biweekly), informing the design and dose selection for the Phase 3 Clarity AD trial.

trials.name: AHEAD 3-45
trials.population: Participants with preclinical Alzheimer's disease and elevated amyloid, and those with early preclinical AD and intermediate amyloid
trials.primary_endpoint: A45 Trial: Change From Baseline in Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) Score at Week 216

related_evidence.description: Primary results of the Clarity AD Phase 3 trial demonstrating efficacy and safety of lecanemab in early Alzheimer's disease.
FDA grants traditional approval to Leqembi (lecanemab) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence for the document's central claims is robust and well-validated by peer-reviewed literature. The Phase 3 Clarity AD trial (NCT03887455) successfully met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant 27% reduction in clinical decline on the CDR-SB over 18 months, with strong performance across secondary endpoints measuring amyloid clearance and cognitive function. This confirmed the target engagement and dose-finding data from the earlier Phase 2b Study 201 (NCT01767311). Due to these definitive effect sizes and high-quality validated endpoints, lecanemab received traditional FDA approval in 2023. Ongoing related trials, such as AHEAD 3-45, are actively expanding the investigation of this drug's mechanism into preclinical Alzheimer's populations.
discrepancies: The document states that lecanemab 'will demonstrate superiority' as a planned evaluation, but the trial has since completed its core 18-month phase and officially published positive results confirming this superiority.

The registry accurately reflects that no native results are posted on the ClinicalTrials.gov platform ('Results posted: false'), but the core trial results are extensively published in peer-reviewed literature (NEJM) and formed the basis for its full regulatory approval.
